presentation_elements_in_florida_model.why: Fixed form wording ('Coverage is provided where a premium or limit...'). Contract/form language, versioned with the form, not policy data.
Fixed form wording introducing the deductible section.
Section headings partition one coverage_limit concept. DC groups the same coverages differently.
Grouping of percent, basis, and computed amount into one display line. The concept is one deductible row; the group is layout.
'Coverage A' is a reference to another coverage, printed as text. Derived label.
How a zero or bundled premium is displayed. Florida prints 'Included'; DC prints no premium column.
No dollar sign on negative credits (assumption 19) is formatting.
Florida prints '3/28/20 to 3/28/2021'; DC spells out months; Socotra prints 'd MMM YYYY'. One policy_period concept.
Configured metadata placed in a header. Socotra's example hard-codes it in {% header %}.
Publisher wrapper, already excluded by the analyzer prompt.
Three dwelling facts on one line. The facts are concepts; the single line is layout.

semantic_key_drift.method: Each model's semantic keys were mapped to concept ids through a hand-written alias table. Keys with no concept are listed as unmapped.
semantic_key_drift.caveat: The alias table was written after seeing the keys, so it measures how much drift a concept layer could absorb, not how well a model would pick concept ids unaided.
